fields.path: An example request file (JSON array of quote objects) relative to the project root. A dry-run takes each table's schema from its declared column types, so a new API Input needs no preview; running the pipeline reads the tables from snapshots that previewing the node builds.
fields.tables: One entry per frame the request yields. Each emitting table is an output of the node, named by its label; downstream edges pick one with source_handle set to that label.
fields.tables[].path: The array the table iterates: "$[:]" for the top-level quotes, "$[:].drivers[:]" for an array nested in each quote.
fields.tables[].label: The frame name, unique in the node, used as the source_handle of edges out of this table.
fields.tables[].emit: true to output the table as a frame.
fields.tables[].row_id_column: The table column that identifies each row, or null.
fields.tables[].columns: {name, path, type, status, selected, levels} per column: name is the frame column, path the JSONPath under the table path ("$[:].vehicle.value" reads a nested object field), type one of int, float, str, bool, date, status "Confirmed", selected true, levels null or the allowed values.

configs.name: minimal
configs.intent: A flat quote request with an id, driver age and vehicle value.

configs.name: realistic
configs.intent: A nested request: a quotes frame reading a nested vehicle object, and a drivers frame from each quote's drivers array.
